#### 1. congenital multicore myopathy with external ophthalmoplegia  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.754)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-2672351, Reactome:R-HSA-5578775)

**Proposed mechanism:** RYR1 (HGNC:10483) —DISRUPTS→ Skeletal muscle excitation-contraction coupling (REACT:R-MUS-163269); Skeletal muscle excitation-contraction coupling (REACT:R-MUS-163269) —LEADS_TO→ Muscle weakness (HP:0001324); Skeletal muscle excitation-contraction coupling (REACT:R-MUS-163269) —LEADS_TO→ Myopathy (HP:0003198). Disruption of the RYR1 gene impairs skeletal muscle excitation-contraction coupling, leading to muscle weakness and myopathy, which are common features of both central core myopathy and congenital multicore myopathy with external ophthalmoplegia.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of distinct, non-overlapping functional consequences of RYR1 variants in the two diseases, or evidence that RYR1 is not the primary causal gene for one of the diseases. _(variant: Exome sequencing data from gnomAD showing the presence of pathogenic variants in RYR1 at a frequency > 0.01% in the general population would call into question its role as a rare disease gene.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism involving RYR1 in these myopathies could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting skeletal muscle function that benefit patients with both conditions.

#### 2. King-Denborough syndrome  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.754)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-2672351, Reactome:R-HSA-5578775)

**Proposed mechanism:** RYR1 variant associated with Central Core Myopathy (HGNC:10483) —DISRUPTS→ Ryanodine Receptor 1 (HGNC:10483); Ryanodine Receptor 1 (HGNC:10483) —DISRUPTS→ Altered calcium handling in skeletal muscle; Altered calcium handling in skeletal muscle —LEADS_TO→ Central core formation (HP:0003700); Altered calcium handling in skeletal muscle —LEADS_TO→ Muscle weakness (HP:0001324); RYR1 variant associated with King-Denborough Syndrome (HGNC:10483) —DISRUPTS→ Ryanodine Receptor 1 (HGNC:10483); Ryanodine Receptor 1 (HGNC:10483) —DISRUPTS→ Abnormal calcium release and excitation-contraction coupling; Abnormal calcium release and excitation-contraction coupling —LEADS_TO→ Susceptibility to malignant hyperthermia (HP:0003701); Abnormal calcium release and excitation-contraction coupling —LEADS_TO→ Muscle weakness (HP:0001324). Both central core myopathy and King-Denborough syndrome arise from mutations in the RYR1 gene, which encodes a critical calcium channel in muscle. Different types of RYR1 mutations lead to distinct alterations in calcium handling, resulting in the characteristic phenotypes of each disease, but converging on the central role of RYR1 in muscle function.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of distinct, non-overlapping sets of RYR1 variants exclusively associated with either central core myopathy or King-Denborough syndrome, with no shared variants exhibiting different functional consequences. _(variant: rs72559925)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared molecular basis of these myopathies, despite differing functional consequences of RYR1 mutations, can inform therapeutic strategies targeting calcium handling pathways to alleviate muscle weakness and other symptoms in both conditions.
